seeds.title: Split lane and worktree lifecycle models
seeds.statement: Treat lane lifecycle and worktree lifecycle as related but non-identical so orchestration lineage can persist independently of concrete worktree status.
evidence: The shard explicitly recommends treating lane lifecycle and worktree lifecycle as related but non-identical.
It distinguishes lane as orchestration lineage object and worktree as concrete Git/filesystem backing object.

seeds.title: Keep lane states while defining worktree states
seeds.statement: Retain the current lane-state vocabulary and define a separate concrete worktree posture vocabulary for Source Control display and operations.
evidence: The lane vocabulary list is presented as still right and should be kept.
The shard proposes a worktree-first state posture including live, dirty, conflict, orphaned, recovering, retained, archived, and removed.

seeds.title: Disambiguate cleanup actions semantically
seeds.statement: Recover, archive, prune, and remove should be separate actions with distinct meanings instead of interchangeable cleanup labels.
evidence: The shard says recover/archive/prune/remove must not blur together.
It assigns explicit meanings where recover is reconcile, archive preserves historical browsing, prune targets policy-eligible stale items, and remove is explicit destructive live-backing removal.

seeds.title: Gate cleanup using lineage-aware checks
seeds.statement: Archive/prune/remove eligibility should be determined by active ownership, recovery dependency, restore targeting, conflict workflows, and lineage dependencies rather than age alone.
evidence: The shard states cleanup must be gated by more than age.
It enumerates pre-checks such as no active-run ownership, no unresolved recovery dependency, no required safe-point restore targeting, and no lineage operation requiring the live object.

seeds.title: Route blocked items to retained or restoring
seeds.statement: When cleanup gates fail, objects should stay in retained/suspect/restoring states rather than being marked cleanup_eligible.
evidence: The shard directly states objects should remain retained, suspect, or restoring when blocking conditions hold.
It contrasts transition candidates into cleanup_eligible versus retained for review and investigation scenarios.

seeds.title: Preserve historical lineage after live removal
seeds.statement: Archive/prune/remove must never erase historical lane/worktree lineage from History, Ledger, or graph-linked inspection.
evidence: The shard states historical lane/worktree records must survive archive, prune, and remove.
It explicitly says live cleanup must never erase run/lane/worktree lineage from History, Ledger, or graph-linked inspection.

seeds.title: Maintain Orchestrator vs Source Control boundary
seeds.statement: Orchestrator should own lane-pool truth and policy context while Source Control stays worktree-first and compact with filters for retained and historical states.
evidence: The shard states Orchestrator owns lane-pool truth and cleanup posture in execution context.
It states Source Control owns concrete worktree actions and should default to compact current/live rows with filters for retained, cleanup-eligible, and archived/removed history.

seeds.title: Require stronger confirmation for destructive actions
seeds.statement: Confirmation strength should scale with risk, with prune/remove generally strong and blocked-lineage removal approaching hard-gate behavior.
evidence: The shard maps archive to light or strong depending on state.
It says prune/remove should usually be strong and remove on blocked/recovery lineage may approach hard_gate.

seeds.title: Normalize glossary for rewrite-critical terms
seeds.statement: Glossary ownership should be extended to emerging Orchestrator concepts and high-risk term pairs to prevent cross-surface semantic drift.
evidence: The shard says Glossary is lagging and lists rewrite-critical terms needing canonical ownership (e.g., lane, lane pool, worktree, superseded, stale_historical, trust states).
It flags risky distinctions like lane vs worktree, history vs ledger, and archive vs remove vs prune that require explicit central definitions.

seeds.title: Reduce live clutter without deleting truth
seeds.statement: The cleanup model should reduce operational clutter while preserving the historical object model and exact lineage needed for audit and recovery.
evidence: The shard warns that without a split model the UI may either delete useful historical truth or keep too much live clutter forever.
It emphasizes cleanup should reduce live clutter without erasing the historical object model.
